extracted.subtask_short: Verifying claims via two-layer fact/assumption evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Determining whether a claim's constituent facts are correct AND whether the underlying assumption/inference it relies on actually holds, using a source-tiered evidence-gathering process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-layer test: factual accuracy of components plus validity of inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Fact's process starts by carefully establishing what claim is actually being made — including the claim's underlying assumption, not merely its surface wording. A claim can be built from factually correct individual facts while still being misleading or incorrect as an overall point — i.e., the truth of the constituent facts does not guarantee the truth of the claim they are assembled to support. The checking process must evaluate both: the evidence cited in the claim itself (are the specific numbers/facts asserted actually correct), and the underlying assumption or inference the claim relies on (does the correct evidence actually establish the broader point being made using it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare PolitiFact's "Half True: partially accurate but takes things out of context" category — evidence can "match" a claim's literal sub-facts while still failing to support the claim's overall thrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the claimant directly for source and right of reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the source of a claim is self-evident, Full Fact's process is to contact the claimant directly to ask about their source and to gather any additional information needed to understand it, and to give them a right of reply before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-source rule and primary-source preference for central claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Fact aims to provide links to primary sources for all factual assertions wherever possible. It aims to provide at least two sources to verify the central claim of any given fact-check, unless there is only one relevant source available. It explicitly prefers linking to data tables, legal documents, or other primary sources rather than to press releases or executive summaries of statistical releases — i.e., when a press release characterizes an underlying dataset, Full Fact's practice is to go around the press release and cite the dataset itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a topic falls outside the researching staff's own expertise, they contact outside subject-matter experts rather than relying solely on their own reading of primary documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory independent second-reviewer step before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Every piece Full Fact publishes is reviewed by another researcher before it goes live, specifically to check that it is correct, impartial, and clearly written. For politically sensitive topics, Full Fact's Director additionally reviews the piece before publication, adding a second, more senior layer of review precisely where the risk of bias or reputational consequence is highest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide links to all sources so readers can independently check the claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Fact states that it provides links to all sources so that readers can check what has been said for themselves and draw their own conclusions.
